For a degree with no oriented simplices, C^k(K;A) is the group of functions from the empty set, hence the zero cochain group; the alternating coboundary and cocycle quotient still make sense. No nonzero genuine observable is inferred from an empty observable sector; the character clause expressly assumes O nonzero.
Statement: the definition includes p=0 and explicitly permits non-Abelian zero-form groups with representation-valued local charges.

Statement: the model may have no nontrivial charge sectors; the definition does not assert a nontrivial action.

risk_review.notes: Read the entire current Definition and its sole direct supplier def-aqft-topological-defect. Checked nonempty group/identity, 0<=p<d including p=0 and p=d-1, total fusion and crossing order, full insertion/background covariance and effectiveness. Discrete cochains have delta^2=0 by cancellation; the quotient is by coboundaries, with relative boundary conventions explicitly model-supplied. Differential characters are defined on all smooth integral cycles, not only curvature; applying the boundary identity to cycles gives 2pi-integral periods, and Stokes shows exact shifts preserve holonomy. Integral-period large shifts preserve holonomy by definition. Flat data are retained and boundary coupling is conditional. Compared GKSW section 3, Bhardwaj sections 2.2.1 and 4.1, and Cheeger-Simons section I definition (PDF p.3); the latter uses cubic chains and degree k on k-cycles, while this explicitly declared simplicial convention uses degree p+2 on p+1 cycles and exponential normalization. No assertion of general gauging, continuum existence, or empirical certainty; no diagram or confirmed defect.

citations.quote:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, an integer $p$ with $0\le p<d$, and a smooth $d$-dimensional spacetime manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. A selected model $\mathcal T$ specifies its spacetime structure and boundary conditions; field configuration space, field bundles, regularity and admitted sectors; observables and their supports; complete admissible insertion inputs, including decorated defects and networks, and their correlation functionals with an explicit normalization; and, when present, its action, regulator, measure, unit system and charge normalization. No such data are inferred from a familiar theory name.

Use the preceding topological-defect definition with its exact content: a defect is model-specified field, operator or boundary-condition data on a closed embedded support, and it is topological when every declared correlator is invariant under each admissible isotopy that transports its data, avoids other insertions and preserves boundary data. For this symmetry, each defect is an endodefect insertion in the same selected model; the model supplies parallel fusion and the induced action on its admitted observables and backgrounds. A support $\Sigma$ is the image of a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ from a manifold without boundary, with closed image in the interior $M^\circ$.

A **group-like $p$-form global symmetry** of $\mathcal T$ consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group $G$, required to be Abelian when $p>0$, and an assignment $g\mapsto U_g(\Sigma)$ of invertible topological symmetry defects to the allowed closed supports $\Sigma$ of dimension $d-p-1$ and codimension $p+1$. For every support and every ordered pair $g,h\in G$, the model supplies parallel fusion $\star$ and the fusion is defined, with

$$U_e(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T},\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_h(\Sigma)=U_{gh}(\Sigma),\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)=U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)\star U_g(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}.$$

Crossing $U_g$ induces a bijection $\rho_g$ on the model's complete typed insertion data, including other defects and their decorations, and a bijection $b\mapsto\beta_g(b)$ on the admissible combined background and boundary data. Both preserve types, supports, algebraic relations and admissibility. With $I$ any complete insertion list and $C_{\mathcal T}$ its model-supplied correlator, covariance means

$$
C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_g(b);\rho_g(I))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;I).
$$

This includes lists with any model-admitted decorated networks, not only ordinary observables. The model specifies crossing junctions and label transport on that domain. Use the convention that crossing $U_g\star U_h$ means crossing $U_h$ and then $U_g$; fusion-action compatibility is the group-action law $\rho_e=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\circ\rho_h$, $\beta_e=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_{gh}=\beta_g\circ\beta_h$. The group $G$ is **effective**: if two elements induce identical crossing automorphisms on every admitted observable and background and give identical actions in every admitted correlator, then they are equal. A group element labels a transformation, not the charge of an observable.

The positive-form restriction selects ordinary local invertible symmetry defects: in codimension at least two, two nearby parallel defects can exchange order in a transverse disk while avoiding other insertions. When decorated transport identifies their crossing and background actions, topologicality and fusion identify the actions of $gh$ and $hg$, and effectiveness gives $gh=hg$. This is the local exchange argument; it does not assert that arbitrary wrapped supports or networks on a topologically nontrivial spacetime can be exchanged. In particular, electric and magnetic flux operators constructed from networks with charged junctions can have a mixed commutator on torsion cycles without changing either ordinary local Abelian label group. Such global network operations are not silently included as a non-Abelian positive-form group in this definition. At $p=0$ no Abelian restriction is imposed.

A **genuine $p$-dimensional observable** is an observable supported on a closed embedded $p$-dimensional submanifold whose definition is independent of an attached higher-dimensional support. Its symmetry action is defined by moving a symmetry defect across it, with the model specifying the resulting junction or operator action. For $p>0$, if crossing by every $U_g$ preserves the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C O$ for a nonzero genuine observable $O$, write the scalar action as $\chi_O(g)O$. If the resulting map $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous homomorphism in a model where $G$ is Abelian, call $\chi_O$ the character charge of $O$; it is an element of $\widehat G$. This definition does not assert scalarity, continuity or multiplicativity for every observable. For $p=0$, local observables may carry higher-dimensional representations of a non-Abelian group; the representation label is distinct from the group element implementing a transformation. For a locally compact Hausdorff Abelian group $A$, write its character group as $\widehat A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(A,U(1))$, with pointwise multiplication. Here $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, so every character value and its argument are dimensionless.

A **background** for a symmetry is nondynamical model data, not summed over. For a finite Abelian group $A$, fix a triangulation $K$ of $M$ and let $C^k(K;A)$ be the group of functions from oriented $k$-simplices to $A$, with orientation reversal acting by negation. Its coboundary is the alternating sum over faces,

$$
(\delta c)([v_0,\ldots,v_{k+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c([v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_{k+1}]).
$$

Since $\delta^2=0$ by pairwise cancellation of twice-deleted faces, a discrete $(p+1)$-form background with no higher-group mixing is a cocycle $B\in C^{p+1}(K;A)$ modulo $B\mapsto B+\delta\Lambda$ for $\Lambda\in C^p(K;A)$. Relative cochains or boundary-fixed gauge transformations are used when required by the model's boundary conditions. If other backgrounds mix with $B$, the model must give the modified cocycle and gauge-transformation laws.

For a continuous $U(1)^r$ $p$-form symmetry, use the following global differential-character model. For $k\geq0$, let $C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)$ be the abelian group of finite integer sums of restrictions to the standard oriented $k$-simplex of smooth maps defined on a neighborhood of that simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of face maps, and let $Z_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)=\ker\partial$. For a smooth $k$-form $\omega$, set $\int_c\omega=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\int_{\Delta^k}\sigma^*\omega$ when $c=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\sigma$. A normalized degree-$(p+2)$ $U(1)$ differential character is a pair $(\check b,H)$ consisting of a group homomorphism $\check b:Z_{p+1}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)\to U(1)$ and a smooth closed real $(p+2)$-form $H$ such that

$$\check b(\partial c)=\exp\!\left(i\int_c H\right)\quad\text{for every }c\in C_{p+2}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z).$$

Indeed, taking $c=z$ for a cycle $z$ gives $\check b(0)=1=\exp(i\int_zH)$, so $\int_zH\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. A $U(1)^r$ background is an $r$-tuple of such characters and curvatures. The character records holonomy on every smooth integral $(p+1)$-cycle, including flat holonomy data that the curvature alone does not record. An optional local presentation on a contractible $V\subset M$ is a smooth potential $B_V\in\Omega^{p+1}(V)$ with $dB_V=H|_V$ and with character values on cycles $z$ in $V$ given by $\check b(z)=\exp(i\int_zB_V)$. The global pair is the background datum, so no choice of local overlap or lower-overlap variables is additional model data; local presentations represent the same background exactly when they specify the same pair $(\check b,H)$. In a global-potential presentation $B\in\Omega^{p+1}(M)$ with $H=dB$, this includes small transformations $B\mapsto B+d\Lambda$ for smooth $p$-forms $\Lambda$ and large shifts $B\mapsto B+\eta$ by smooth closed $(p+1)$-forms $\eta$ whose periods are in $2\pi\mathbb Z$; for nontrivial sectors the equality-of-pair rule is the complete gauge-equivalence condition. If fixed boundary data are imposed, the selected model specifies the corresponding relative chain and character convention. The unit system and all coefficients in background couplings remain model inputs. The model must define its correlators in these backgrounds; this definition asserts neither that every symmetry admits such a coupling nor that the symmetry can be gauged.

derivations.claim: Total group-like fusion gives $U_g\star U_h=U_{gh}$ and $U_h\star U_g=U_{hg}$ on a common support for arbitrary $g,h\in G$.

Fusion-action compatibility in the stated raw data gives $\chi_O(gh)O=\rho_{gh}(O)=\rho_g(\rho_h(O))=\chi_O(h)\chi_O(g)O$. Since the scalar values commute and $O\ne0$, $\chi_O(gh)=\chi_O(g)\chi_O(h)$. The identity action gives $\chi_O(e)=1$.

By [A1], the exchange identifies the composite crossing bijections $\rho_g\circ\rho_h$ and $\rho_h\circ\rho_g$ and the composite background maps on the complete admitted domain. Topologicality in the stated raw data also makes their correlator actions identical. Fusion compatibility and effectiveness in the stated raw data therefore identify the group labels $gh$ and $hg$, so $gh=hg$ for arbitrary $g,h\in G$. This argument uses no Hilbert-space or operator hypothesis.

Unitary conjugation preserves the operator norm, so $\|O\|=\|V_gOV_g^{-1}\|=\|\chi_O(g)O\|=|\chi_O(g)|\|O\|$. Because $O\ne0$, its norm is positive and $|\chi_O(g)|=1$. By [A3], the resulting homomorphism is continuous; hence $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is continuous.

By the definition of $\widehat G$ in [F1], using Abelianity from step 2.1, $\chi_O\in\widehat G$. The proof establishes Abelianity for this single group under the specified local exchange hypothesis and does not imply that distinct higher-form symmetry groups commute jointly.

Step 2.2: the group identity has character value one; no nontrivial group element is required.
Statement: the operator is bounded and nonzero; Step 2.2 uses nonzeroness before cancelling O.
Statement: 1<=p<d makes support dimension d-p-1 nonnegative and codimension at least two.
Statement: group, model, operator, junction action and exchange isotopies are explicit hypotheses; no choice principle is used.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle for a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, with $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$. A supplied principal connection is a smooth, right-invariant complement $TP=VP\oplus H$, where $VP=\ker d\pi$; write $v:TP\to VP$ for the projection along $H$, and let $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$ be its vertical-valued curvature. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$ and $p\in P$, define the fundamental vertical vector $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The orbit differential $\zeta_p: \mathfrak g\to V_pP$, $Z\mapsto Z_P(p)$, is a linear isomorphism, as proved below. Define the **principal connection 1-form** by

$$\omega_p(X):=\zeta_p^{-1}(v_pX),\qquad X\in T_pP.$$

Then $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$ for every fixed $g\in G$. Conversely, a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form with the reproduction and equivariance properties determines the principal connection $H=\ker\omega$. The converted vertical curvature $\kappa_H:=\omega\circ K_H$ is a $\mathfrak g$-valued alternating 2-form; its equality with the Cartan curvature is established in the curvature lemma.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle with a principal connection form $\omega$ associated to $H$, using $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_G(tZ)$ for the right action. For Lie-algebra-valued forms use the graded bracket defined by alternating shuffle and the Lie bracket; in degree one, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$. Define

$$\Omega_\omega:=d\omega+\frac12[\omega\wedge\omega],\qquad D_\omega\eta:=d\eta+[\omega\wedge\eta].$$

Then $\Omega_\omega$ is horizontal and $\operatorname{Ad}$-equivariant, and $\Omega_\omega=\omega\circ K_H$ for the imported vertical-valued curvature $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$. For any trivializing cover with smooth sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=s_i^*\Omega_\omega$. On an overlap, let $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to G$ be the smooth map determined by $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$, and write $\theta_L(g_{ij})=g_{ij}^*\theta_L$ for the left Maurer–Cartan form. Then

$$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+\theta_L(g_{ij}),\qquad F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i],\qquad F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i,\qquad D_{A_i}F_i=0,$$

where $D_{A_i}\eta:=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The transition equations concern changes of local sections; they do not identify an arbitrary map $M\to G$ with a global automorphism of a nontrivial bundle.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, possibly with boundary. For $k\ge1$, $c\in C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb R)$ and $\omega\in\Omega^{k-1}(M)$, define integration over a chain by the finite linear sum of its simplex integrals. Then
$$\int_c d\omega=\int_{\partial c}\omega.$$
The zero chain has integral zero. In degree zero the boundary is zero; no degree-minus-one form is required by this statement.

derivations.claim: The Lie algebra of $U(1)$ is Abelian, so $[A_i\wedge F_i]=0$; its adjoint action is trivial, so the local forms $F_i$ agree on overlaps. Applying [F2] gives the global curvature $F$ and $dF_i=0$ in every chart away from the external line, hence $dF=0$ there.

Fix an admitted compact $\Sigma$. On its finite good cover, the local connection forms satisfy $A_j-A_i=d\theta_{ij}$ by the transition formula in [F2]. On a triple overlap, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ implies $\theta_{ij}+\theta_{jk}-\theta_{ik}=2\pi n_{ijk}$ for an integer $n_{ijk}$; on fourfold overlaps these integers satisfy $n_{jkl}-n_{ikl}+n_{ijl}-n_{ijk}=0$. Refine the chosen finite triangulation so each oriented triangle lies in one cover set and label each triangle by such a set. Stokes [F3] on each triangle writes its curvature integral as a boundary integral of its local $A_i$. For an interior edge shared by triangles labelled $i$ and $j$, the two opposite boundary contributions combine to $\int_e(A_i-A_j)=-\int_e d\theta_{ij}$, an endpoint difference of the chosen transition lift. Summing the edge endpoint differences around a vertex gives a signed cyclic sum of transition angles; its exponential is the product of transition functions around that cycle, equal to $1$ by $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$. Hence each vertex contribution lies in $2\pi\mathbb Z$, and $\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma F$ is a signed sum of integers. This uses the ordinary compact $U(1)$ bundle sectors and is independent of the separate magnetic-line boundary condition [A1].

Suppose the swept chain $V$ is disjoint from $C$. By [F3] and step 1.1, $\int_{\Sigma_1}F-\int_{\Sigma_0}F=\int_{\partial V}F=\int_VdF=0$. The defining exponential is therefore pointwise unchanged by every admitted source-free isotopy. Multiplying by any other admitted insertion functions preserves that equality, and applying the model's linear functional $\mathcal L_{C,m,b}$ proves equality for every complete correlator. Thus the surface operator is topological in this sector.

At each intersection, projection $T_{x_j}W\to N_{x_j}C$ has orientation sign $\epsilon_j$ by the Example's convention; excision reverses the boundary orientation on the linking sphere, giving $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0-\sum_j\epsilon_jS_j^2$. The punctured chain lies in the source-free region, so [F3] and step 1.1 give $0=\int_VdF=\int_{\Sigma_1}F-\int_{\Sigma_0}F-\sum_j\epsilon_j\int_{S_j^2}F$. The flux boundary condition in [A1] therefore gives $\int_{\Sigma_1}F-\int_{\Sigma_0}F=2\pi m I(W,C)$.

Write $N_\Sigma=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_\Sigma F\in\mathbb Z$ by step 2.1. Replacing $\widetilde\alpha$ by $\widetilde\alpha+2\pi k$ multiplies $U_\alpha(\Sigma)$ by $e^{2\pi i kN_\Sigma}=1$, so the operator depends only on $\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$. For representatives $\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta$, pointwise multiplication gives $U_\alpha(\Sigma)U_\beta(\Sigma)=U_{\alpha+\beta}(\Sigma)$; also $U_0(\Sigma)=1$ and $U_{-\alpha}(\Sigma)$ is its inverse. Thus these operators define the claimed $U(1)$ fusion action on every admitted closed surface.

Substitution into the definition of $U_\alpha$ yields $U_\alpha(\Sigma_1)T_m(C)=e^{i\widetilde\alpha m I(W,C)}T_m(C)U_\alpha(\Sigma_0)$. Multiplying this pointwise relation by all other admitted insertion functions and applying $\mathcal L_{C,m,b}$ gives the same phase relation for every complete correlator, without dividing by any possibly zero correlator. For one positively oriented linking, the phase is $e^{i\alpha m}$, which is independent of the representative of $\alpha$.

Because $m\in\mathbb Z$, $\chi_m(e^{i(\alpha+2\pi)})=\chi_m(e^{i\alpha})$, so the formula defines a map on $U(1)$; it is continuous, multiplicative, and sends $1$ to $1$. By the character-charge convention in [F4] and the unit-linking crossing phase in step 3.2, $\chi_m$ is the line's one-form charge and lies in $\widehat{U(1)}$.

Applying step 3.2 to the admitted unit-charge probe $T_1$ gives crossing phase $\chi_1(e^{i\alpha})=e^{i\alpha}$. If two group elements induce the same crossing action on every admitted observable and background, they induce the same action on $T_1$; since $T_1$ is nonzero, their phases coincide, so the group elements are equal in $U(1)$. Thus the stated symmetry action is effective as required by the preceding definition.

If $m=0$ or $\alpha=0$, the linking phase is one. Reversing the orientation of the line changes $m$ to $-m$, and reversing the swept-chain orientation changes $I$ to $-I$, so the formula respects the declared orientation convention. No equation of motion, observation, or continuum-existence conclusion is used.

citations.quote:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, an integer $p$ with $0\le p<d$, and a smooth $d$-dimensional spacetime manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. A selected model $\mathcal T$ specifies its spacetime structure and boundary conditions; field configuration space, field bundles, regularity and admitted sectors; observables and their supports; complete admissible insertion inputs, including decorated defects and networks, and their correlation functionals with an explicit normalization; and, when present, its action, regulator, measure, unit system and charge normalization. No such data are inferred from a familiar theory name.

Use the preceding topological-defect definition with its exact content: a defect is model-specified field, operator or boundary-condition data on a closed embedded support, and it is topological when every declared correlator is invariant under each admissible isotopy that transports its data, avoids other insertions and preserves boundary data. For this symmetry, each defect is an endodefect insertion in the same selected model; the model supplies parallel fusion and the induced action on its admitted observables and backgrounds. A support $\Sigma$ is the image of a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ from a manifold without boundary, with closed image in the interior $M^\circ$.

A **group-like $p$-form global symmetry** of $\mathcal T$ consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group $G$, required to be Abelian when $p>0$, and an assignment $g\mapsto U_g(\Sigma)$ of invertible topological symmetry defects to the allowed closed supports $\Sigma$ of dimension $d-p-1$ and codimension $p+1$. For every support and every ordered pair $g,h\in G$, the model supplies parallel fusion $\star$ and the fusion is defined, with

$$U_e(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T},\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_h(\Sigma)=U_{gh}(\Sigma),\qquad U_g(\Sigma)\star U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)=U_{g^{-1}}(\Sigma)\star U_g(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}.$$

Crossing $U_g$ induces a bijection $\rho_g$ on the model's complete typed insertion data, including other defects and their decorations, and a bijection $b\mapsto\beta_g(b)$ on the admissible combined background and boundary data. Both preserve types, supports, algebraic relations and admissibility. With $I$ any complete insertion list and $C_{\mathcal T}$ its model-supplied correlator, covariance means

$$
C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_g(b);\rho_g(I))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;I).
$$

This includes lists with any model-admitted decorated networks, not only ordinary observables. The model specifies crossing junctions and label transport on that domain. Use the convention that crossing $U_g\star U_h$ means crossing $U_h$ and then $U_g$; fusion-action compatibility is the group-action law $\rho_e=\mathrm{id}$, $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\circ\rho_h$, $\beta_e=\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta_{gh}=\beta_g\circ\beta_h$. The group $G$ is **effective**: if two elements induce identical crossing automorphisms on every admitted observable and background and give identical actions in every admitted correlator, then they are equal. A group element labels a transformation, not the charge of an observable.

The positive-form restriction selects ordinary local invertible symmetry defects: in codimension at least two, two nearby parallel defects can exchange order in a transverse disk while avoiding other insertions. When decorated transport identifies their crossing and background actions, topologicality and fusion identify the actions of $gh$ and $hg$, and effectiveness gives $gh=hg$. This is the local exchange argument; it does not assert that arbitrary wrapped supports or networks on a topologically nontrivial spacetime can be exchanged. In particular, electric and magnetic flux operators constructed from networks with charged junctions can have a mixed commutator on torsion cycles without changing either ordinary local Abelian label group. Such global network operations are not silently included as a non-Abelian positive-form group in this definition. At $p=0$ no Abelian restriction is imposed.

A **genuine $p$-dimensional observable** is an observable supported on a closed embedded $p$-dimensional submanifold whose definition is independent of an attached higher-dimensional support. Its symmetry action is defined by moving a symmetry defect across it, with the model specifying the resulting junction or operator action. For $p>0$, if crossing by every $U_g$ preserves the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C O$ for a nonzero genuine observable $O$, write the scalar action as $\chi_O(g)O$. If the resulting map $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous homomorphism in a model where $G$ is Abelian, call $\chi_O$ the character charge of $O$; it is an element of $\widehat G$. This definition does not assert scalarity, continuity or multiplicativity for every observable. For $p=0$, local observables may carry higher-dimensional representations of a non-Abelian group; the representation label is distinct from the group element implementing a transformation. For a locally compact Hausdorff Abelian group $A$, write its character group as $\widehat A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(A,U(1))$, with pointwise multiplication. Here $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, so every character value and its argument are dimensionless.

A **background** for a symmetry is nondynamical model data, not summed over. For a finite Abelian group $A$, fix a triangulation $K$ of $M$ and let $C^k(K;A)$ be the group of functions from oriented $k$-simplices to $A$, with orientation reversal acting by negation. Its coboundary is the alternating sum over faces,

$$
(\delta c)([v_0,\ldots,v_{k+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c([v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_{k+1}]).
$$

Since $\delta^2=0$ by pairwise cancellation of twice-deleted faces, a discrete $(p+1)$-form background with no higher-group mixing is a cocycle $B\in C^{p+1}(K;A)$ modulo $B\mapsto B+\delta\Lambda$ for $\Lambda\in C^p(K;A)$. Relative cochains or boundary-fixed gauge transformations are used when required by the model's boundary conditions. If other backgrounds mix with $B$, the model must give the modified cocycle and gauge-transformation laws.

For a continuous $U(1)^r$ $p$-form symmetry, use the following global differential-character model. For $k\geq0$, let $C_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)$ be the abelian group of finite integer sums of restrictions to the standard oriented $k$-simplex of smooth maps defined on a neighborhood of that simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of face maps, and let $Z_k^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)=\ker\partial$. For a smooth $k$-form $\omega$, set $\int_c\omega=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\int_{\Delta^k}\sigma^*\omega$ when $c=\sum_\sigma n_\sigma\sigma$. A normalized degree-$(p+2)$ $U(1)$ differential character is a pair $(\check b,H)$ consisting of a group homomorphism $\check b:Z_{p+1}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z)\to U(1)$ and a smooth closed real $(p+2)$-form $H$ such that

$$\check b(\partial c)=\exp\!\left(i\int_c H\right)\quad\text{for every }c\in C_{p+2}^\infty(M;\mathbb Z).$$

Indeed, taking $c=z$ for a cycle $z$ gives $\check b(0)=1=\exp(i\int_zH)$, so $\int_zH\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. A $U(1)^r$ background is an $r$-tuple of such characters and curvatures. The character records holonomy on every smooth integral $(p+1)$-cycle, including flat holonomy data that the curvature alone does not record. An optional local presentation on a contractible $V\subset M$ is a smooth potential $B_V\in\Omega^{p+1}(V)$ with $dB_V=H|_V$ and with character values on cycles $z$ in $V$ given by $\check b(z)=\exp(i\int_zB_V)$. The global pair is the background datum, so no choice of local overlap or lower-overlap variables is additional model data; local presentations represent the same background exactly when they specify the same pair $(\check b,H)$. In a global-potential presentation $B\in\Omega^{p+1}(M)$ with $H=dB$, this includes small transformations $B\mapsto B+d\Lambda$ for smooth $p$-forms $\Lambda$ and large shifts $B\mapsto B+\eta$ by smooth closed $(p+1)$-forms $\eta$ whose periods are in $2\pi\mathbb Z$; for nontrivial sectors the equality-of-pair rule is the complete gauge-equivalence condition. If fixed boundary data are imposed, the selected model specifies the corresponding relative chain and character convention. The unit system and all coefficients in background couplings remain model inputs. The model must define its correlators in these backgrounds; this definition asserts neither that every symmetry admits such a coupling nor that the symmetry can be gauged.

Let $d\ge2$, $1\le p<d$, and let $\mathcal T$ be a selected model with the following raw group-like defect data. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group, with no Abelianity assumption. On every admitted closed codimension-$(p+1)$ support, supply invertible topological endodefects $U_g$ with total parallel fusion $U_g\star U_h=U_{gh}$, transparent identity and inverses. Supply crossing bijections $\rho_g$ on complete typed insertion data and background/boundary bijections $\beta_g$, preserving types, supports, algebraic relations and admissibility, with $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\circ\rho_h$, $\beta_{gh}=\beta_g\circ\beta_h$ and identity actions at $e$. Require covariance $C_{\mathcal T}(\beta_g(b);\rho_g(I))=C_{\mathcal T}(b;I)$ for every complete admitted insertion list $I$ and background $b$, including decorated networks, and invariance of each declared correlator under admissible isotopies transporting all defect data. Require effectiveness: equal crossing actions on the complete domain, equal background maps, and equal actions in all admitted correlators imply equal group labels. These are the model, topologicality, fusion, crossing, covariance and effectiveness data of the preceding symmetry definition, with its extra positive-form Abelianity restriction deliberately withheld. Suppose that for every $g,h\in G$ and every allowed configuration of remaining insertions and fixed data, the model admits two parallel copies of their codimension-$(p+1)$ symmetry supports inside a contractible neighborhood with a disk spanned by two independent normal directions, and an admissible isotopy exchanging their order without intersecting any other insertion or changing boundary or model data. Require that the model-supplied transport along this isotopy identifies the two composite crossing bijections on all complete typed insertion data and the two composite background maps; that is, it identifies $\rho_g\circ\rho_h$ with $\rho_h\circ\rho_g$ and $\beta_g\circ\beta_h$ with $\beta_h\circ\beta_g$. Then $G$ is Abelian, so these data satisfy also the positive-form group restriction in that definition.

For the separate character conclusion, assume additionally that the crossing action has a unitary Hilbert-space realization: there are a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a group homomorphism $V:G\to U(\mathcal H)$, with $V_e=I$ and $V_{gh}=V_gV_h$, such that crossing $U_g$ acts on bounded linear operators by $O\mapsto V_gOV_g^{-1}$. Let $O\in B(\mathcal H)$ be a nonzero genuine $p$-dimensional operator, where $B(\mathcal H)$ is the space of bounded linear operators with norm $\|O\|:=\sup_{\|\psi\|=1}\|O\psi\|<\infty$. Call $O$ **simple for this result** if crossing each $U_g$ sends it to a scalar multiple $\chi_O(g)O$, and assume the map $g\mapsto\chi_O(g)\in\mathbb C$ is continuous. Then $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous character, so the charge of $O$ belongs to the Pontryagin dual $\widehat G=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,U(1))$. Neither conclusion is asserted for $p=0$; the character conclusion also makes no claim for nonscalar crossing actions.

derivations.claim: For every $\sigma,\tau\in S_3$ and basis vector $e_j$, $\rho(\sigma)\rho(\tau)e_j=e_{\sigma(\tau(j))}=\rho(\sigma\tau)e_j$, so $\rho$ is a representation by unitary permutation matrices. With $s=(12)$ and $t=(23)$, $\rho(s)\rho(t)e_1=e_2$ while $\rho(t)\rho(s)e_1=e_3$; hence $S_3$ is non-Abelian.

Every permutation fixes $e_1+e_2+e_3$, and permutes coordinates, so it preserves the sum-zero subspace $V_2$. These subspaces intersect only at zero and have dimensions one and two, so $\mathcal H=\mathbb C(e_1+e_2+e_3)\oplus V_2$.

Let $r=(123)$ and $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/3}$. The vectors $v_+=(1,\zeta,\zeta^2)$ and $v_-=(1,\zeta^2,\zeta)$ form eigenlines for $\rho(r)$ with distinct eigenvalues $\zeta^2$ and $\zeta$. The transposition $s=(12)$ sends $v_+$ to $\zeta v_-$ and $v_-$ to $\zeta^2v_+$. Any invariant line for $S_3$ would have to be one of the two eigenlines of $\rho(r)$, but neither is preserved by $\rho(s)$; thus $V_2$ has no nonzero proper invariant subspace and is irreducible.

For insertions whose cyclic time order is fixed, moving a symmetry point without crossing another insertion leaves the ordered matrix product unchanged; the trace correlation is therefore unchanged. This applies to arbitrary mixed lists of matrices and other defects. Simultaneous conjugation of all factors telescopes to conjugation of their product, so cyclicity gives $\frac13\operatorname{Tr}(\rho(g)O_1\cdots O_n\rho(g)^{-1})=\frac13\operatorname{Tr}(O_1\cdots O_n)$, including all defect factors. The singleton boundary datum is fixed. Adjacent defect factors multiply as $U_\sigma U_\tau=U_{\sigma\tau}$, independently of separation, proving fusion in every complete correlator. The operator assignment $U_\sigma(t)=\rho(\sigma)$ is therefore topological and has the full symmetry covariance in this finite model. Since $p=0$, the hypothesis $p\ge1$ of [F2] fails, so no Abelianity conclusion applies to $S_3$.
The two summands in step 1.2 are representation spaces, while the elements $s,t\in S_3$ in step 1.1 are transformations; their distinct roles are explicit in the action $\rho(\sigma)$.
